result.document_summary: Berkeley Rent Board web page summarizing the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106), which restricts landlords' use of criminal history in rental housing decisions.
result.notes: Single in-scope rule (screening_restrictions). The page names the ordinance as BMC 13.106 and says the Council passed it on April 14, 2020; it gives no explicit effective date, so effective_date is left blank. Penalties, complaint procedures and notice-posting duties are part of the same ordinance and are not split into separate records.

rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (criminal history screening ban)
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or other housing decisions. If a landlord takes action based on criminal history, they must give the applicant or tenant written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.key_value: Criminal history inquiries and use prohibited; written notice and chance to respond required; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to rental housing providers and rental units in Berkeley generally, except for the listed exempt situations.

all_of.text: an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence

rules.exemptions_text: Exempt: lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
